Mood: idle.> The pens are quiet, and the boy is home with his father. That is enough good news for one day.
<long pause>
A: <A woman aged105. Ancient, dry, papery voice with age-cracked creak, light breathy quaver and frail breath support. Soft low-mid register. Unhurried short phrases with small natural pauses. Warm, wry rural English manner; perfectly lucid and self-possessed. Clearly very elderly, not a young actress speaking slowly, not the firm resonant guard captain. Mood: sad.> The boy reached my fire, and I sent him home to his father. Poor old bear. A hundred winters, and the last was the coldest. Keep the claw; there is nothing else down there to carry home.
<long pause>

<long pause>

Mood: idle.> A grey bear is taking goats from the pens, and a fisher's boy is missing. The cave mouth is below Maud's hut on the burned bank. Will you search for him and put an end to the bear?
<long pause>
A: <Mature female guard captain, late forties to fifties. Low, flat Northern English delivery. Grounded chest resonance, lightly weathered texture, restrained grief and calm clipped authority. No youthful brightness, frailty or theatrical growling. Speak only the dialogue. Mood: idle.> Aye. When the Hearth fails, the strong eat the weak, and everyone starves in the end. We have to find out what's happening to it.
<long pause>
A: <Mature female guard captain, late forties to fifties. Low, flat Northern English delivery. Grounded chest resonance, lightly weathered texture, restrained grief and calm clipped authority. No youthful brightness, frailty or theatrical growling. Speak only the dialogue. Mood: idle.> The Stranger knows. I see how they watch the road east. When the time comes, we make them talk.
<long pause>
A: Twenty gold. My own. Now choose.
<long pause>
B: I had hoped you would turn back. I cannot yield the gate.
